key_insight: A large language model–built toxicity resource showed that cancer therapy side effects are shaped by both clinical context and inherited genetic risk, enabling prediction of who is more likely to be harmed.
clinical_relevance: This work supports pre-treatment toxicity risk stratification across cancer therapies, including identifying patients at higher risk for specific adverse events before starting treatment.
method: Built MSK-Tox from EHR text using an LLM to capture toxicity incidence, timing, and grade.
Analyzed six key adverse events across cancer types and treatment regimens.
Tested clinical predictors and germline associations to model toxicity risk.
evidence_signal: The study used data from more than 50,000 patients and evaluated six representative toxicities, finding distinct clinical and genetic determinants for each.
watch_item: The findings are promising but will need external validation and careful integration into clinical workflows before use in treatment decisions.
paper_title: Population-Scale Precision Safety in Oncology Reveals Clinical and Genetic Determinants of Systemic Therapy Toxicity
